old: "In regulatory contexts, Hungarian relies on impersonal predicates + infinitive: *tilos belépni* ('entry prohibited'), *kötelező viselni* ('mandatory to wear'), *szabad használni* ('permitted to use'), *nem szabályos eljárni* ('improper to proceed')."
new: "You know *tilos*, *szabad* and *kötelező* + infinitive from A2 Unit 23. Regulations, notices and house rules use the same impersonal predicates + infinitive; new here is *szabályos* ('proper, in order'): *tilos belépni* ('entry prohibited'), *kötelező viselni* ('mandatory to wear'), *szabad használni* ('permitted to use'), *nem szabályos eljárni* ('improper to proceed')."
why: A2 Unit 23 taught szabad/tilos/kötelező + infinitive: recap, not new

old: "The suffix *-andó/-endő* attaches to verb stems to form adjectives expressing that an action must or should be performed: *a megoldandó feladat* ('the task to be solved'), *a betartandó szabály* ('the rule to be observed'), *a fizetendő összeg* ('the amount payable')."
new: "You know the future participle *-andó/-endő* from B1 Unit 27. It attaches to verb stems to form adjectives expressing that an action must or should be performed: *a megoldandó feladat* ('the task to be solved'), *a betartandó szabály* ('the rule to be observed'), *a fizetendő összeg* ('the amount payable')."
why: -andó/-endő is future-participle-ando, B1 Unit 27 (b1-14-01-a): recap, not new

old: "*Felelősséget vállal vmiért* ('takes responsibility for sth' - causal-final *-ért*), *felelős vmiért* ('responsible for sth'), *számon kéri a hibákat* ('holds sb accountable for errors')."
new: "You know *felelősséget vállal* from B1 Unit 45 and verbs governing *-ért* from A2 Unit 8: *felelősséget vállal vmiért* ('takes responsibility for sth'), *felelős vmiért* ('responsible for sth'). New here is *számon kéri a hibákat* ('holds sb accountable for errors')."
why: felelősséget vállal is Unit 45, -ért government A2 Unit 8: recap

old: "*Kell* (objective or general necessity), *muszáj* (urgent, inescapable physical or practical pressure), *kénytelen* (reluctantly forced by external circumstances: *kénytelen volt elismerni*)."
new: "You know *kell* and *muszáj* from A1 Unit 24 and *kénytelen* from B1 Unit 19. Compare their shades: *kell* (objective or general necessity), *muszáj* (an urgent, inescapable must), *kénytelen* (reluctantly forced by external circumstances: *kénytelen volt elismerni*)."
why: kell/muszáj A1 Unit 24, kénytelen B1 Unit 19: recap, not new

old: "Formal, legal agreements replace casual *ha* with elevated conditional conjunctions: *amennyiben* ('in the event that / in so far as'), *feltéve, hogy...* ('provided that...'), *abban az esetben, ha...* ('in the case that...')."
new: "You know *amennyiben* ('in the event that') from A2 Unit 13. Formal, legal agreements use it instead of casual *ha*, and add *feltéve, hogy...* ('provided that...') and *abban az esetben, ha...* ('in the case that...')."
why: amennyiben is ha-clause, A2 Unit 13: recap; new are feltéve, hogy / abban az esetben, ha

old: "*Ezzel szemben* ('in contrast to this / on the contrary'), *ugyanakkor* ('at the same time'), *holott* ('whereas / although in reality')."
new: "You know *ezzel szemben* ('in contrast to this') from B1 Unit 21 and *ugyanakkor* ('at the same time') from B1 Unit 35. New here is *holott* ('whereas / although in reality'), which says that the opposite is true: *A cég azt állítja, hogy betartotta a szabályokat, holott megszegte őket.*"
why: ezzel szemben Unit 21, ugyanakkor Unit 35 known; holott had no example
